appliedScenePlan.nextHook: safety crews will respond by marking and labeling the leaking material with formal H- und P-Sätze hazard stickers
appliedScenePlan.stillPrompt: documentary phone-photo close-mid of a cluttered Kaufhaus aisle: wooden crates and a small refrigerated display newly labeled with old-high-german script 'fleisc' stenciled in rough black ink, several catalog leaflets stuck to crate faces, red seep stains spreading across paper and concrete. Exposed ventilation ducts, cable trays and an industrial cart in the background; plain white partitions and mirrored steel column visible. Harsh uneven fluorescent and cold window light, modest dynamic range, slight wide-angle distortion, natural dust, workers' gloved hands in frame affixing labels; gritty, unvarnished realism.
appliedScenePlan.videoPrompt: animate only environmental and object motion from the still: a slow drip of red forming and falling, stain expanding across the leaflet and concrete, a gloved hand pressing a label onto a crate, faint condensation sweeps on the refrigerated glass, fluorescent flicker and handheld camera micro-motion; keep movement limited to objects, fluids and human actions shown in the start frame.
appliedScenePlan.cameraCue: eye-level mid shot (approx. 35mm equiv.), slightly tilted to emphasize the spreading stain and stenciled 'fleisc' label in the center.

appliedScenePlan.title: Labeling the Leak
appliedScenePlan.event: A safety team arrives and begins affixing bright hazard stickers and handwritten H- and P-codes to the crates and leaflets; they tape off the aisle with yellow hazard tape and place a small open spill kit and a fine white absorbent powder next to the leaking crate.
appliedScenePlan.consequence: yellow quarantine tape stretched across the aisle, multiple H-/P-stickered crates and a small mound of white absorbent powder with one set of small boot prints leading away
appliedScenePlan.nextHook: the quarantine draws a crowd of the public who will press and test the barrier (Public)
appliedScenePlan.stillPrompt: phone-photo documentary of the same Kaufhaus aisle now cordoned with yellow hazard tape: close-to-wide angle showing crates with adhesive H- and P-stickers, a spill kit open and a small mound of absorbent white powder on cardboard, a clipboard with handwritten H-/P-codes, mirrored steel column and exposed ceiling ducts visible. Work lights and fluorescent fixtures create mixed warm/cold lighting, slight lens distortion and natural dust; modest dynamic range and imperfect exposure.
appliedScenePlan.videoPrompt: animate tape fluttering slightly in the AC, a LED hazard panel on a clipboard blinking intermittent H/P codes, a faint puff of white powder when a worker brushes it, tape vibration from distant footfalls, handheld camera micro-motion; restrict animation to the physical traces, labels, and tools in the scene.
appliedScenePlan.cameraCue: high handheld angle over the yellow tape at chest height (approx. 50mm equiv.), focusing on the absorbent powder, stickers and boot prints while keeping the barricade in the frame.

appliedScenePlan.title: Pressing Against the Tape
appliedScenePlan.event: A mixed crowd of shoppers and on-site workers arrives and begins pressing against and pulling at the quarantine tape; some film on phones, one person angrily rips down a leaflet, and a dropped backpack skids across concrete, colliding with a crate and knocking loose a hazard sticker which flutters away.
appliedScenePlan.consequence: a torn and sagging quarantine tape, a knocked-clean crate with a dislodged hazard sticker fluttering on the floor, a spilled backpack with receipts and product flyers scattered
appliedScenePlan.nextHook: the disorder focuses attention and draws a more violent rupture in the atrium, coinciding with an explosive event and a hulking presence (Terrorism leads to visible rupture)
appliedScenePlan.stillPrompt: documentary phone-photo of the Kaufhaus crowd pressing at the yellow hazard tape: mixed people (shoppers in coats, site workers in vests) crowding a taped-off aisle, phones held up, anxious faces, one person tearing a leaflet. A backpack lies open on the concrete with receipts and product flyers spilled; fluorescent fixtures, exposed ducts and mirrored steel columns frame the scene. Natural imperfect exposure, slight wide-angle distortion, dust and grit visible.
appliedScenePlan.videoPrompt: animate crowd motion: hands gripping and tugging the tape until it sags, phones glowing and recording, the backpack sliding and its contents scattering, voices and distant shouted phrases, the dislodged hazard sticker fluttering on the concrete; limit animation to the crowd and object-level motion already present.
appliedScenePlan.cameraCue: shoulder-level tight handheld among the crowd (approx. 35mm equiv.), focusing on hands gripping tape and the moment the backpack knocks the crate so the torn tape and fluttering sticker are revealed.

appliedScenePlan.title: Rupture in the Atrium
appliedScenePlan.event: A sudden sharp pop and a brief smoky flare from a small improvised device in a display case coincide with people ducking and the alarm starting; already present in the scene, a squat, mottled creature stands near a mirrored steel column — visible from the first frame — people scatter, shelving topples and a conspicuous scorch gouge appears on the concrete floor near the column.
appliedScenePlan.consequence: a blackened scorch gouge on the concrete beside the steel column, toppled metal shelving, smoke and a scattered pile of torn leaflets and flyers around the creature's feet
appliedScenePlan.nextHook: the damaged atrium and fear trigger frantic consumption behavior and improvised markets as people try to salvage or trade goods (Gut / Konsum)
appliedScenePlan.stillPrompt: phone-photo documentary frame of the unfinished Kaufhaus atrium at the moment after a small explosive pop: wide-angle, dusty concrete with visible sweep marks and a fresh black scorch gouge on the floor. The creature is already visible at the beginning — a squat, low-slung figure with a matte, mottled hide dusted with construction debris, oiled tendon-like limbs, and a neutral, standing posture beside a mirrored steel column; it occupies the midground and is not posed theatrically. Around it people run and toppled metal shelving leans on its side, smoke plumes drift up, an emergency exit sign flickers, exposed ducts and cable trays overhead, practical fluorescent and window light mixed, modest dynamic range, ordinary phone-photo imperfection. The image must not imply the creature caused the device — it is present and observed. Keep gritty documentary realism.
appliedScenePlan.videoPrompt: start from the still described above and animate only environmental and crowd motion: smoke plumes slowly drift upward and disperse, emergency lights and fluorescents flicker, people run and stumble past the creature, a brochure flutters and skids across the scorch mark, dust falls from displaced ceiling tiles, alarms oscillate and distant footsteps echo. The creature remains visually static as shown in the start frame and should not be animated to enter, move into frame, or change form.
appliedScenePlan.cameraCue: low-angle wide handheld (approx. 24–28mm equiv.) from behind a fallen rack, positioned to show the scorch gouge in the foreground, the creature near the column in midground, and fleeing people in the background so the rupture is revealed.

appliedScenePlan.title: Markets of Panic
appliedScenePlan.event: In the immediate aftermath, some people begin salvaging and trading goods from toppled racks; improvised stalls form from shelving and crates, price tags are scribbled on leaflets and taped to damaged columns, and small exchanges of cash and products happen as a makeshift market forms — the creature remains visible in the background near a column, a passive presence amid the barter.
appliedScenePlan.consequence: an improvised stall made from a toppled shelf with handwritten price tags stuck to a damaged column, people exchanging goods and money, and the creature partially obscured behind the column as part of the background
appliedScenePlan.nextHook: the scene resolves the visible residue into commerce: torn leaflets become price tags and the damaged atrium becomes a temporary market (fresh term Gut/Konsum absorbed into the space)
appliedScenePlan.stillPrompt: phone-photo documentary of the Kaufhaus converted into an improvised market: people clustered around a toppled metal shelf used as a stall, items laid out on cardboard, hastily scribbled price tags taped to a damaged steel column and on old 'fleisc' leaflets, warm practical lights mixed with cold window light, modest dynamic range and gritty detail. The creature is visible in the start frame, partly obscured behind the column at the edge of the stall, dusty and still, not posed; shoppers bargain and a security guard attempts to supervise. Keep the unfinished interior cues (exposed ducts, cable trays, construction clutter, fluorescent fixtures) and phone-photo imperfections.
appliedScenePlan.videoPrompt: from the start frame animate only human-scale and environmental motion: hands exchanging cash and goods across the makeshift stall, price tags fluttering, a loose leaflet skittering along the concrete into the foreground, flicker of practical lights and a distant siren, small dust motes drifting. The creature remains visually static as shown in the start frame and should not be animated to enter, move, or transform.
appliedScenePlan.cameraCue: mid-level handheld (approx. 35–50mm equiv.) over the improvised stall, shallow focus on the exchange with the creature blurred but visible behind the damaged column, revealing how commerce has repurposed the damage.
